name: Daily ATR-stopped time-series momentum
entry_long: At completed 00:00 UTC daily close, if C[d]/C[d-60]>1 and C[d]>SMA200(daily close), enter long next hourly open; one position per coin.
entry_short: At daily close if C[d]/C[d-60]<1 and C[d]<SMA200(daily close), enter short next hourly open.
exit: Exit next hourly open after daily momentum changes sign or after 30 completed days; no same-bar reversal.
stop: At entry place stop 3.0*ATR14(daily) from entry; never widen; stop executes on real price path.
why_it_should_work: Underreaction may let large directional moves persist across weeks. ATR-defined stops adapt dollar risk to recent volatility. This exact rule is unverified.

name: Daily 20/60/120 return vote

entry_short: Enter short if at least 2 of 3 <0 and daily C<SMA200.
exit: Exit at next hourly open when vote drops below 2 in position direction; maximum hold 45 days.

why_it_should_work: Agreement among horizons may reduce reliance on a single noisy signal. Letting strong winners run is consistent with time-series momentum research. This exact rule is unverified.

why_it_should_work: Directional trends sometimes continue under moderate realized volatility. Excluding the highest-volatility regimes may avoid the most disorderly moves but can also remove the best winners. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market: A Comprehensive Analysis under Realistic Assumptions (Han, Kang & Ryu, 2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds strong time-series but almost no cross-sectional crypto momentum under more realistic assumptions.

evidence.source: Regime changes in Bitcoin GARCH volatility dynamics (2019)
evidence.what_it_found: Documents changing BTC volatility regimes and better one-day VaR forecasts from regime-switching GARCH.

evidence.source: Volatility-Managed Portfolios (Moreira & Muir, 2017)
evidence.what_it_found: Volatility scaling improved factor portfolios in conventional assets; does not validate a crypto trading signal.

fails_when: Volatility spikes at profitable breakout onset or crashes quickly reverse.
cost_sensitivity: medium: time in trade and funding can erode the edge

name: Daily tail-candle continuation
entry_long: At UTC daily close, daily log return>+2*sd of prior 30 completed daily log returns and close at least 80% up daily high-low range; long if EMA50(daily)>EMA200.
entry_short: Return<-2*prior 30d sd and close in bottom 20% of range; short if EMA50<EMA200.
exit: Exit after 3 completed daily closes or earlier when daily close moves below midpoint of signal candle (long) / above (short).
why_it_should_work: A rare abnormal return may reflect information being incorporated across several days. There is also documented short-term reversal, so continuation is expressly uncertain. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets (Zaremba et al., 2021)
evidence.what_it_found: Large illiquid coins show daily reversal, while the most liquid major coins show daily momentum.

evidence.source: Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both (Wen et al., 2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Reports regime-dependent intraday momentum and reversal; sensitive to jumps, liquidity, and events.

fails_when: Climactic daily moves reverse and event news is digested immediately.
cost_sensitivity: low: rare trades with potentially large excursions

name: Three-coin 7-day relative-strength spread
entry_long: At each Monday 00:00 UTC, rank 7d returns among BTC,ETH,SOL; if leader return - laggard return>0.05 AND BTC daily C>SMA100, long leader and short laggard simultaneously, dollar-neutral.
entry_short: The short leg is the lowest 7d-return coin in the same entry; no standalone short. Tie BTC then ETH then SOL.
exit: Exit both legs after 7 days or when leader/laggard ranks reverse on daily close.
stop: If sum of both legs marked-to-market P&L reaches -1% of account flatten both; cap combined notional at 1.5x equity.
target: Target spread P&L +2% account or none if stop first.
why_it_should_work: Relative strength might persist even when market direction is unstable. Recent realistic crypto research finds little robust cross-sectional alpha, so this is a low-priority falsification test. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market: A Comprehensive Analysis under Realistic Assumptions (Han, Kang & Ryu, 2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds strong time-series but almost no cross-sectional crypto momentum under more realistic assumptions.

evidence.source: Cross-Sectional Momentum in Cryptocurrency: A Net-of-Costs Replication (Arefev, 2026, preprint)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds specified recent perpetual-futures cross-sectional momentum spreads not distinguishable from zero after costs.

fails_when: Relative spread snaps back; the three-asset sample overfits; hedges are imperfect.
cost_sensitivity: high: two full round trips (~0.32% notionals in two legs) plus differential funding

name: ETH/BTC ratio 4h breakout
entry_long: Compute R=ETH-USD spot close/BTC-USD spot close on aligned completed 4h bars. If R closes above prior 30-bar maximum and ETH 4h EMA50[t]>EMA50[t-1], long ETH future and short equal-USD BTC future.
entry_short: If R closes below prior 30-bar minimum and ETH 4h EMA50[t]<EMA50[t-1], short ETH and long equal-USD BTC.
exit: Exit both if ratio crosses its EMA20(4h) against position or after 14 days.
stop: Stop both legs when completed 4h log(ETH/BTC) moves 2.5*mean(abs(delta log(ETH/BTC)), prior 14 completed 4h bars) against entry; stop uses close-only synthetic series, not fabricated intrabar ratio highs.
why_it_should_work: ETH leadership relative to BTC may persist during crypto rotation. Futures basis and two-leg expenses make spot-ratio evidence unreliable until checked on actual futures. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Pair trading strategies in the cryptoassets market: a cointegration framework (2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds some cointegrated crypto pairs profitable OOS; does not establish that BTC/ETH or SOL/ETH are stable pairs.

evidence.source: Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency (Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu, 2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Identifies market, size and momentum factors across a broad crypto universe; not a three-coin strategy proof.

evidence.source: Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market: A Comprehensive Analysis under Realistic Assumptions (Han, Kang & Ryu, 2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds strong time-series but almost no cross-sectional crypto momentum under more realistic assumptions.

fails_when: Ratio regimes change, funding basis diverges, correlation breaks.
cost_sensitivity: high: two futures legs and nonstationary spread

name: SOL/ETH ratio 4h breakout
entry_long: At 4h close compute log(SOL close/ETH close). Long SOL and short equal-USD ETH if log-ratio closes above prior 40-bar maximum and SOL 4h EMA50>EMA200.
entry_short: Short SOL and long ETH if log-ratio closes below prior 40-bar minimum and SOL 4h EMA50<EMA200.
exit: Exit both if log-ratio crosses EMA20(log-ratio 4h) against position or after 14 days.
stop: Stop both legs if ratio log-price falls/rises 3*Wilder ATR14 of log ratio (ATR built from aligned 4h log closes using absolute close-to-close changes).
why_it_should_work: Relative leadership may track differences in adoption or beta for stretches of time. SOL may be more volatile, so hedging by equal dollars does not eliminate market risk. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Pair trading strategies in the cryptoassets market: a cointegration framework (2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds some cointegrated crypto pairs profitable OOS; does not establish that BTC/ETH or SOL/ETH are stable pairs.

evidence.source: Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market: A Comprehensive Analysis under Realistic Assumptions (Han, Kang & Ryu, 2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds strong time-series but almost no cross-sectional crypto momentum under more realistic assumptions.

fails_when: SOL beta shock, broad market squeeze, funding costs on both legs.
cost_sensitivity: high: two legs, substantial relative volatility, divergent basis

name: ETH/BTC rolling residual reversion
entry_long: Every closed 4h bar fit OLS log(ETH)=a+b*log(BTC) using preceding 180 completed 4h bars only; compute current residual and z=(residual-mean(training residual))/sd(training residual). If z<-2 and ADF test (constant included, 1 lag, 5% critical value) of the 180 preceding training residuals p<0.05 estimated before signal, long ETH and short b beta-adjusted BTC.
entry_short: If z>+2 with same pre-signal ADF test, short ETH and long b beta-adjusted BTC.
exit: Exit both at |z|<0.5 on a completed 4h bar or after 7 days.
stop: Flatten both if |z|>3.5 or pair P&L<-1% account; no stop loosening.
why_it_should_work: A statistically stationary residual might revert when the spread deviates substantially. Neither cointegration nor an economic return is established for this pair without point-in-time tests. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Pair trading strategies in the cryptoassets market: a cointegration framework (2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds some cointegrated crypto pairs profitable OOS; does not establish that BTC/ETH or SOL/ETH are stable pairs.

fails_when: Cointegration fails, spread trends, model refit repaints historical trades.
cost_sensitivity: high: two legs, higher round-trip fee burden; stationary assumption fragile

name: Weekend 4h compression break
entry_long: At Sunday 23:59 UTC use completed Saturday 00:00–Sunday 23:59 UTC high/low; at Monday closed 4h bar long if close>weekend high and 4h EMA50>EMA200.
entry_short: At Monday closed 4h bar short if close<weekend low and EMA50<EMA200.
exit: Exit Friday 16:00 America/New_York or 4h close back inside weekend range, whichever first.
stop: Stop min(3*ATR14(4h), 0.75*(weekend high-weekend low)) away from fill.
why_it_should_work: Weekend liquidity and activity often decline, possibly creating narrower reference ranges. Breakout profits after weekends are not supported by a stable documented directional anomaly. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Revisiting seasonality in cryptocurrencies (2024)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds no robust directional return seasonality but consistently lower weekend activity.

evidence.source: Bitcoin on Wall Street Time (2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds growing US-session concentration and quieter weekends in BTC activity.

fails_when: Monday range breaks reverse or weekend range is unusually wide.
cost_sensitivity: medium: sparse weekly entries; transaction costs still matter

name: Hourly RSI2 dip with daily trend
entry_long: At 1h close, last completed daily EMA50>EMA200, 1h RSI2<5 for 2 consecutive completed bars, and 1h ATR14/C>0.003; long next hourly open.
entry_short: Daily EMA50<EMA200, 1h RSI2>95 twice and ATR14/C>0.003; short.
exit: Exit if RSI2 crosses 60 long / 40 short or 12 completed hours, whichever first.
why_it_should_work: Short-term overreaction can rebound within a durable trend. Prior paper losses show a high win rate does not imply positive expectancy after fees. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both (Wen et al., 2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Reports regime-dependent intraday momentum and reversal; sensitive to jumps, liquidity, and events.

evidence.source: Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets (Zaremba et al., 2021)
evidence.what_it_found: Large illiquid coins show daily reversal, while the most liquid major coins show daily momentum.

fails_when: Persistent falling knife, weekend inactivity, many small wins versus large stops.
cost_sensitivity: high: short holds and narrow profit opportunity relative to 0.16%

name: US-hour 4h follow-through
entry_long: At 16:00 UTC daily on latest fully closed hourly bars, compute 12:00–16:00 UTC log return. Long if return>+0.01 and completed 4h EMA50>EMA200.
entry_short: Short if return<-0.01 and 4h EMA50<EMA200.
exit: Exit at 00:00 UTC next day or if completed 1h close crosses EMA20(1h) against trade.
why_it_should_work: Some published intraday continuation evidence concentrates in more active sessions. A specified fixed-time entry prevents post-hoc selection, but the chosen hours may not replicate. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Bitcoin intraday time series momentum (2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Reports intraday BTC momentum conditional on high-volume or high-volatility sessions; different execution assumptions.

evidence.source: Periodicity in Cryptocurrency Volatility and Liquidity (Hansen, Kim & Kimbrough, 2024)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds recurrent hourly, weekly and intrahour volatility/volume patterns in BTC and ETH, not directional alpha.

fails_when: Activity peaks without predictable direction; long signal is a late move.
cost_sensitivity: high: day-trade horizon makes all-in fees material

name: Five-minute high-volume range break
entry_long: At completed 5m close, if C>prior 36-bar high, V>2*SMA20(volume), completed 1h EMA50>EMA200 and ATR14(5m)/C>0.002, long.
entry_short: If C<prior 36-bar low, V>2*SMA20(volume), completed 1h EMA50<EMA200 and ATR14/C>0.002, short.
exit: Exit after 24 completed 5m bars or on 5m close crossing EMA20 against trade.
why_it_should_work: High participation on a multi-hour breakout may sustain follow-through. Volume from spot candles remains an imperfect proxy for futures liquidity. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Bitcoin intraday time series momentum (2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Reports intraday BTC momentum conditional on high-volume or high-volatility sessions; different execution assumptions.

evidence.source: Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both (Wen et al., 2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Reports regime-dependent intraday momentum and reversal; sensitive to jumps, liquidity, and events.

fails_when: Breakout is a stop-run, spread widens, or 5m ATR is too small.
cost_sensitivity: high: one of the most cost-sensitive allowed hypotheses

name: Month-boundary daily continuation
entry_long: On UTC day 1 of each month after 00:00 daily close, long if prior calendar-month return>+0.05 and daily C>EMA100.
entry_short: Short if prior calendar-month return<-0.05 and daily C<EMA100.
exit: Exit on UTC day 8 at 00:00 or if daily C crosses EMA20 against trade.
why_it_should_work: Month boundaries could coincide with periodic reallocations, but crypto calendar return anomalies are generally unstable. This is primarily a negative-control seasonal hypothesis. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Revisiting seasonality in cryptocurrencies (2024)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds no robust directional return seasonality but consistently lower weekend activity.

evidence.source: Are day-of-the-week effects in cryptocurrencies real? (Aalipour et al., 2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds calendar-return anomalies localized to a few hours and assets, not persistent day-level effects.

fails_when: A calendar label does not predict directional follow-through; tiny sample count.
cost_sensitivity: low: sparse trades, but no established gross positive expectancy

name: Funding-extreme 4h trend filter
data_needed: OHLCV + historical per-product hourly CFM funding rates + actual futures bars
entry_long: When completed 4h EMA50>EMA200 and last published hourly US-perp funding rate is <=+0.00005 (decimal fraction per hour, equivalent to +0.005%), long.
entry_short: When 4h EMA50<EMA200 and last published funding rate >=-0.00005, short.
exit: Exit after completed 4h EMA50/EMA200 cross against position or 7 days.
stop: Stop 3*ATR14(4h futures candles; if not available, spot proxy with execution validation).
why_it_should_work: Avoiding expensive carry may improve the net result of an otherwise valid trend. Funding is also an endogenous measure of crowding and may vary rapidly. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Coinbase US perpetual-style futures funding rate mechanism
evidence.what_it_found: Funding is calculated hourly from the futures/spot premium; its direction varies.

evidence.source: Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market: A Comprehensive Analysis under Realistic Assumptions (Han, Kang & Ryu, 2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds strong time-series but almost no cross-sectional crypto momentum under more realistic assumptions.

fails_when: Funding flips between hourly observations; restrictive entry eliminates winning moves.
cost_sensitivity: medium: may save carry, but requires actual historical hourly funding

name: Open-interest supported 4h breakout
data_needed: OHLCV + point-in-time hourly open interest for each CFM contract
entry_long: At closed 4h bar, C exceeds high of prior 30 completed 4h bars and total futures open interest has risen >=5% over prior 24h using last published point-in-time observations; long.
entry_short: At 4h C below prior 30-bar low and 24h futures open interest rises >=5%; short.
exit: Exit on 4h close crossing EMA20 against trade or 10 days.
why_it_should_work: Open-interest expansion might distinguish new futures positioning from forced position closing. Whether that indicates continuation depends on venue coverage and direction of subsequent liquidation. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market: A Comprehensive Analysis under Realistic Assumptions (Han, Kang & Ryu, 2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds strong time-series but almost no cross-sectional crypto momentum under more realistic assumptions.

evidence.source: More to cryptos than bitcoin: A GARCH modelling of heterogeneous cryptocurrencies (Fung et al., 2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Documents volatility clustering, heavy tails, and persistent volatility across cryptoassets; not trading-rule profits.

fails_when: Open interest surges at tops; OI aggregate has publication lag or inconsistent coverage.
cost_sensitivity: medium: longer moves might justify fees, but new data and carry are essential

name: Extreme funding contrarian 1h
data_needed: OHLCV + historical hourly per-product CFM funding
entry_long: At 1h close, if funding percentile of last published CFM hourly funding among previous 720 published hours >=95 AND hourly RSI14>=75, enter short.
entry_short: If funding percentile <=5 AND hourly RSI14<=25, enter long.
exit: Exit on hourly RSI14 returning to 50 or after 48h.
why_it_should_work: Extreme carry may signal crowded directional positions that unwind. Reversals against strong momentum are risky and the empirical edge for these thresholds is unverified. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Coinbase US perpetual-style futures funding rate mechanism
evidence.what_it_found: Funding is calculated hourly from the futures/spot premium; its direction varies.

evidence.source: Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both (Wen et al., 2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Reports regime-dependent intraday momentum and reversal; sensitive to jumps, liquidity, and events.

fails_when: Crowded trends persist, funding stays extreme, stop repeatedly hit.
cost_sensitivity: high: 1–2 day countertrend trades and funding uncertainty
overlap_with: Hourly RSI2 dip with daily trend

name: Liquidation-shock hourly rebound
data_needed: OHLCV + timestamped historical futures liquidation volume by long/short direction (not currently available)
entry_long: At closed 1h bar, long if timestamped aggregate hourly long liquidations across designated CFM contracts exceed 95th percentile of prior 180d and daily EMA50>EMA200 and hourly RSI14<30.
entry_short: Short if aggregate hourly short liquidations exceed 95th percentile and daily EMA50<EMA200 and RSI14>70.
exit: Exit after RSI14 returns to 50 or after 24 hours.
why_it_should_work: Forced positioning unwinds could create short-term price dislocations. Reliable contract-specific liquidation timestamps and volumes are necessary before this is testable. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both (Wen et al., 2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Reports regime-dependent intraday momentum and reversal; sensitive to jumps, liquidity, and events.

evidence.source: More to cryptos than bitcoin: A GARCH modelling of heterogeneous cryptocurrencies (Fung et al., 2022)
evidence.what_it_found: Documents volatility clustering, heavy tails, and persistent volatility across cryptoassets; not trading-rule profits.

fails_when: Continued forced selling, liquidation data incomplete, publication lag.
cost_sensitivity: high: crisis slippage and frequent stop-outs can exceed the baseline

name: On-chain valuation with daily momentum
data_needed: OHLCV + point-in-time asset-specific MVRV histories with revision timestamps
entry_long: Daily close: long BTC or ETH only when latest point-in-time 7d-average MVRV z-score<0 and daily 20d return>0 and daily C>SMA100.
entry_short: Short only when MVRV z-score>2 and daily 20d return<0 and C<SMA100.
exit: Exit when daily 20d return sign flips or after 45 days.
why_it_should_work: On-chain valuation may indicate market stress or euphoria when combined with price direction. Historical MVRV series may be revised and the signal requires point-in-time chain data. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market: A Comprehensive Analysis under Realistic Assumptions (Han, Kang & Ryu, 2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds strong time-series but almost no cross-sectional crypto momentum under more realistic assumptions.

evidence.source: Time series momentum (Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen, 2012)
evidence.what_it_found: Documents multi-month momentum in traditional liquid futures, not these crypto-specific rules.

fails_when: Valuation decouples from price or on-chain metric is revised.
cost_sensitivity: low: infrequent; funding over weeks is the principal cost

name: Post-FOMC hourly price continuation
data_needed: OHLCV + official point-in-time scheduled FOMC announcement calendar
entry_long: For a scheduled FOMC rate statement on official calendar at 14:00 America/New_York, at end of first completed 14:00–15:00 ET hourly candle go long if its return>+1%, hourly volume>2*SMA20(1h volume), daily EMA50>EMA200.
entry_short: At same bar go short if return<-1%, hourly volume threshold met and daily EMA50<EMA200.
exit: Exit after 4 closed hourly bars or upon 1h EMA20 crossing against position.
stop: Stop 3*ATR14(1h), but reject trade if signal-bar range>6*ATR14(1h) due to extraordinary jump.
why_it_should_work: Scheduled Fed announcements materially increase BTC/ETH volatility, creating a potential follow-through setting. The referenced study does not demonstrate predictable post-event direction or profitable trading. This exact rule is unverified.

evidence.source: Scheduled FOMC statements and intraday macro event risk in cryptocurrency markets (2026)
evidence.what_it_found: Finds markedly greater absolute BTC and ETH price moves and volume around scheduled FOMC statements; not directional predictability.

fails_when: Initial surge immediately reverses, bid/ask widens, tiny annual sample.
cost_sensitivity: high: event spreads and slippage likely exceed normal assumption
